title: Kenyan Coconut Celebration Rice
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: Celebration Coconut Rice is the celebration-scale version of KEN021 (Wali wa Nazi). The technique is identical but the ratio of coconut milk is more generous, and the rice is garnished with toasted coconut, fried onions, and sometimes rose water for important celebrations.

desc: Kenyan Coconut Celebration Rice — wali wa Nazi prepared with extra richness for celebrations. More coconut milk, toasted coconut garnish, and fried onions elevate the everyday coastal rice into the fragrant, glistening centrepiece of the celebration table.
longDesc: Celebration wali wa Nazi is distinguished from everyday coconut rice by its generosity — more coconut milk for a richer result, a toasted coconut garnish, and fried shallots on top. At coastal weddings, Eid celebrations, and birthday feasts, the wali wa Nazi arrives as a fragrant, glistening mountain of rice that signals abundance and joy.
ingredients: 4 cups basmati rice — washed and soaked 30 minutes
½ cup desiccated coconut — dry-toasted until golden
2 shallots — thinly sliced and fried until crispy
equipment: Large heavy pot with tight lid
steps: Combine coconut milk, water, salt, and butter in a large pot. Bring to a boil.
Add rice. Stir once. Return to a boil.
Reduce to the lowest possible heat. Cover tightly.
Cook for 18—20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from heat. Rest covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff gently. Transfer to serving platter.
Top with toasted coconut, crispy shallots, and a dash of rose water if using.
chefTips: More coconut milk than the everyday version — this is the celebration ratio.
The crispy fried shallot garnish is the celebration signature.
Never lift the lid during cooking.
cookingScience: See KEN021 for the full cooking science. The higher coconut milk ratio creates a more emulsified cooking liquid — the fat coats more of the rice grains, producing a silkier, richer result than the everyday proportion.
sustainabilityTips: The garnish ingredients are minimal — the rice itself is the star.
reheating: Steam briefly or microwave with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Basmati rice is lower GI than regular rice.
culturalNote: Celebration wali wa Nazi is the rice dish that tells guests they are valued — the extra coconut milk, the toasted garnish, the fragrant rose water are all signals of hospitality and care that the cook is communicating through food.
